ing: peeled and cut in thin matchsticks
st: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 24 hours, changing the water 3 times. Then simmer it in fresh water for 10 minutes, drain, and flake it, removing skin and bones.
Heat the neutral oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C) and fry the potato matchsticks in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels and salt lightly.
Heat the olive oil in a large wide skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions for 10 minutes until very soft but not browned.
Add the garlic and flaked cod and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the fried potatoes and toss to mix.
Lower the heat, pour in the beaten eggs, and stir gently for 2 minutes until just creamy and barely set. Take off the heat right away; the eggs finish cooking from the heat of the pan.
Season with pepper, taste for salt, and top with the olives and parsley. Serve immediately.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] of the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, the salt and [[6 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Mash the potatoes right in the pot with a masher, or blend with an immersion blender, until the soup is thick and smooth.
Slice the kale into the thinnest ribbons you can; stack the leaves, roll, and cut across.
Brown the chouriço slices in a dry skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes and set aside.
Add the kale to the soup and simmer for 5 minutes only so it stays bright green.
Season with pepper and taste for salt. Ladle into bowls, add the sausage, and drizzle with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.

ing: lager; use broth to skip alcohol
st: Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a saucepan and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the beer, broth, hot sauce, bay leaf and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes until slightly thick, then remove the bay leaf and blend smooth. Keep warm.
Season the steaks with salt and fry in [[1 tbsp]] butter for 2 minutes per side until cooked through. Fry the sausage for 6 minutes until browned and hot in the middle.
Heat the oven broiler. Lay 4 slices of bread on a baking sheet. Top each with ham, a steak, and a piece of sausage.
Add a second slice of bread on each and cover completely with 2 slices of cheese.
Broil for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Fry the eggs in the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter until the whites are set, about 3 minutes.
Place each sandwich on a plate, top with a fried egg, and pour the hot sauce over generously. Serve with fries.
Heat the oven as hot as it will go, at least 475°F (245°C). Butter a 12-cup muffin pan.
Roll up the puff pastry sheet into a tight log and cut 12 even slices. Press each slice flat, then press it into a muffin cup, thinning the sides up the walls.
Whisk the cornstarch with a splash of the milk to make a paste. Heat the rest of the milk, the cream, cinnamon stick and lemon peel in a pan until steaming.
Whisk the sugar and cornstarch paste into the milk and cook, whisking, for 3 minutes until thickened. Remove the cinnamon and peel.
Whisk the yolks in a bowl, then slowly whisk in the hot custard so they do not scramble. Add the vanilla and cool 10 minutes.
Pour the custard into the pastry cups, filling about 3/4 full.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the tops have dark brown blisters and the pastry is crisp.
Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then dust with cinnamon. Best eaten warm the same day.

ing: spatchcocked (backbone removed) or cut in pieces
bird's eye or red Fresno, chopped
st: Blend the chilies, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, vinegar, paprika, oregano, salt and pepper into a rough marinade.
Pat the chicken dry. Cut deep slashes in the thick parts and set aside about a third of the marinade in a clean bowl for serving, and rub the rest all over the chicken.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, up to overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and place the chicken skin side up on a rack in a roasting pan. Alternatively grill over medium heat.
Roast for 45 to 55 minutes, brushing with a little of the used marinade halfway, until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes, then carve.
Serve with the clean reserved marinade spooned over or on the side.

ing: bird's eye or Thai, stems removed
st: Wear gloves and handle the chilies carefully. Roughly chop them with the garlic.
Warm the olive oil with the bay leaf in a small saucepan over low heat for 3 minutes.
Add the chilies and garlic and cook gently for 5 minutes without browning.
Remove the bay leaf and let the mixture cool for 10 minutes.
Add the lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, salt and oregano. Blend to a smooth or slightly rough sauce.
Pour into a clean jar. Taste and add salt or vinegar to balance the heat.
Store in the fridge for up to 2 weeks and use on grilled chicken, fish or fries.
Slice the pork thinly and pound lightly to even thickness.
Mix the garlic, wine, paprika, bay leaves, salt, pepper and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a bowl and add the pork. Turn well to coat.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 3 hours, or overnight.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and the lard in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the pork slices in batches for 2 minutes per side until browned and cooked to 145°F (63°C), adding a splash of marinade at the end.
Pour the remaining marinade into the pan, boil for 3 minutes, then return all the pork to the sauce.
Pile the pork and sauce into the rolls and serve with mustard.
Broil or grill the bell peppers over high heat for 15 minutes, turning, until the skin is black all over.
Put the peppers in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel off the skin, remove seeds, and slice into strips.
Toss the pepper strips with the onion, tomato, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, vinegar and salt to make a salad.
Pat the sardines dry and sprinkle them all over with the coarse salt. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Heat a grill or grill pan until very hot. Brush the sardines with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Grill the sardines for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the skin is charred and the flesh flakes.
Serve whole on slices of bread with the pepper salad and lemon wedges.
Put the beef and pork in a large stockpot with the onion, bay leaves and water to cover. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes until the meats are nearly tender. Add the salt.
Add the chouriço, carrots and turnips and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer 15 minutes. Then add the cabbage wedges and the blood sausage and simmer 10 minutes more until all vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile cook the rice with [[2 cups]] chicken broth in a covered pot over low heat for 18 minutes.
Lift the meats and vegetables onto a large platter and slice the meats and sausages.
Serve with the rice and a ladle of the cooking broth on the side.
Soak the clams in cold salted water for 20 minutes so they release sand, then rinse. Discard any open clams or mussels that do not close when tapped.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaf, paprika and salt and cook 8 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the wine and cook 1 minute.
Pour in [[4.5 cups]] hot stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Nestle in the clams, mussels and shrimp. Cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes until the shells open and the shrimp are pink. Discard any shells that stay closed.
Stir in half of the cilantro; the rice should be soupy. Taste for salt, sprinkle with the rest of the cilantro and serve in bowls.
Mix the pork with the garlic, wine, paprika, bay leaves, salt and pepper. Marinate in the fridge for 2 hours.
Soak the clams in cold salted water for 20 minutes, then rinse well.
Drain the pork, keeping the marinade. Pat the pork dry and brown it in the olive oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes.
Add the marinade and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes until the pork is tender (145°F/63°C minimum).
Meanwhile fry the potato cubes in oil at 350°F (175°C) for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain and salt.
Add the clams to the pork, cover, and cook 5 to 6 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Fold in the fried potatoes and cilantro. Serve with lemon wedges.
Put the rice, [[2 cups]] water, lemon peel, cinnamon stick and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes until the water is mostly absorbed.
Warm the milk in another pan. Add it to the rice a cup at a time, stirring often, letting each addition absorb before adding more.
Stir in the sugar and cook for 5 minutes more over low heat until creamy. Remove the lemon peel and cinnamon stick.
Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl with a ladle of the hot rice to warm them gently.
Pour the yolk mixture into the pot off the heat, stirring constantly, then cook on very low heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until slightly thicker. Do not boil.
Spoon into a serving dish or small bowls and let it cool.
Decorate with ground cinnamon patterns and serve warm or chilled.
